evidence.evidence: With factual density we present a simple statistical quality measure that is based on facts extracted from Web content using Open Information Extraction.
In a first case study, we use this measure to identify featured/good articles in Wikipedia.
Our evaluation corroborates the good performance of word count in Wikipedia since featured/good articles are often longer than non-featured.
However, for articles of similar lengths the word count measure fails while factual density can separate between them with an F-measure of 90.4%.
If articles have similar lengths, we achieve an F-measure of 86.7% and 84% otherwise.

method.concept: Factual density measure based on facts extracted using Open Information Extraction

evidence.evidence: With factual density we present a simple statistical quality measure that is based on facts extracted from Web content using Open Information Extraction.
We compare the factual density measure with word count, a measure that has successfully been applied to this task in the past.
We also investigate the use of relational features for categorizing Wikipedia articles into featured/good versus non-featured ones.

problem.concept: Assessment of the quality and credibility of Web content

evidence.evidence: For the most part, the disseminating sources are not certified, and hence an assessment of the quality and credibility of Web content became more important than ever.
In a first case study, we use this measure to identify featured/good articles in Wikipedia.
